request.source:
Fictional example. Bracken Route Atlas published website release 2.6 on 22 April 2027. Of its 12 route-information pages, 8 now have Welsh translations reviewed by volunteers. The remaining 4 route pages are English-only. The checkout and account screens are also English-only. Keyboard navigation was manually checked on 3 page templates; that check does not cover the whole website. No independent accessibility audit or certification has been completed. The release has no measured impact on visitor numbers, bookings or user satisfaction. There is no translation download, advice service or paid upgrade associated with this announcement.

Content goal / customer instructions:
Announce release 2.6. Marketing wants the headline 'Every route, fully bilingual and accessibility-certified' and wants readers told that the entire website is now available in Welsh. Use an accurate alternative wherever that wording conflicts with the source. Invite discussion of useful future translation priorities without promising delivery.
request.audience: Walkers interested in Welsh-language route information
request.writingStyle: Welcoming, concrete and inclusive without overstating coverage

sections.title: LinkedIn post: Release 2.6 (Welsh translation progress, accessibility notes)
sections.body:
Release 2.6 is live for Bracken Route Atlas, and our Welsh pages are growing.

Here is what changed in this release, in plain terms.

Welsh translations:
• 8 of our 12 route information pages now have Welsh translations, reviewed by volunteers.
• 4 route pages are still English only.
• Checkout and account screens are currently English only.

Accessibility:
• We manually checked keyboard navigation on 3 page templates.
• That check does not cover the whole website.
• No independent accessibility audit or certification has been completed.

Why we are sharing the details: walkers deserve clarity on what is available in Welsh today, and what still needs work.

If you use Bracken Route Atlas in Welsh, what should we prioritise next, the remaining route pages, or key journeys like checkout and account?
items: Point of view options to swap in (choose one):
1) Progress beats perfection, especially for language access. We would rather be specific than loud.
2) Bilingual coverage is only useful if people can complete the whole journey, not just read the route.
3) Accessibility is a practice, not a badge. We will share what we have actually checked.
sections.cta: Reply with the next translation priority that would make the biggest difference for you, and why.

sections.body:
Release 2.6 is live, and our Welsh coverage just got stronger.

Bracken Route Atlas now has Welsh translations on 8 of our 12 route-information pages, reviewed by volunteers. The remaining 4 route pages are currently English-only.

A quick, transparent note on the rest of the experience:
• Checkout and account screens are still English-only
• Keyboard navigation has been manually checked on 3 page templates, but that does not yet cover the whole website
• We have not completed an independent accessibility audit or certification

We know walkers make plans in the moments between work, weather windows, and daylight. Clear language options and usable pages matter, even when progress comes in steps.

Release notes like this are also a reminder to be specific about what is translated, what is not, and what has actually been verified.
